title: 6.25.3 Lab: Trail online
description: Your Trail plays a classmate on another computer: rolls are sent, every roll is checked and applied in onMove, and only the player whose turn it is may roll.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: This is your game from 6.24.3. It plays on one computer; H does nothing yet.

steps.title: A room and a listener
steps.instructions: At the top, add `const JOIN = '';`. At the end of `setup()`, apply every move: `online.onMove((move, seat) => takeTurn(move.roll));`, then `if (JOIN !== '') online.join(JOIN);`. In `draw()`, H hosts with a fresh board: `if (kb.presses('h') && online.status === 'off') { newGame(); online.host(); }`.
hints: Without `newGame()`, turns you played alone before pressing H stay on your board, while your classmate starts on square 0, and the two boards never match.
Add `|| online.status === 'closed'` to the H test if you want H to host again after a room ends.

steps.title: Send the roll, do not apply it
steps.instructions: Where SPACE rolls the die, keep the die in a variable `r`, then: if `online.status === 'off'`, call `takeTurn(r)` as before; otherwise `online.send({ roll: r })`. The roll comes back in `onMove` on both computers.
hints: Online, a roll applied where SPACE is pressed AND in `onMove` moves the token twice on your screen.
If your SPACE line calls `takeTurn(floor(random(1, 7)))` directly, split it: `const r = floor(random(1, 7));` first, then the if.

steps.title: Ignore a move that makes no sense
steps.instructions: Make `onMove` check before it applies: only when `seat === turn`, `winner === -1` and `goodRoll(move.roll)`, where `goodRoll(r)` returns `floor(r) === r && r >= 1 && r <= 6`. A move from the wrong seat, or a roll of 100, is then ignored on every computer, and the boards still agree.

steps.title: Only your seat rolls
steps.instructions: Write `myTurn()`: offline it is always true; online it is true only when `online.status === 'ready'` and `online.seat === turn`. SPACE rolls only when `myTurn()` is true. Let R start a new game only when `online.status === 'off'`, so one computer cannot reset its board alone; online, the win message says `' Run again and host a new room to play again'` instead.
hints: Seat 0 is the host and `players[0]`; seat 1 is the classmate and `players[1]`.

steps.title: Show the room, then play
steps.instructions: In `drawTop()`, show the room code while `online.status === 'waiting'`, `'Online, you are ' + players[online.seat].name` when it is `'ready'`, `'Room closed: H for a new one'` when it is `'closed'`, and a hint that H hosts when it is `'off'`. When it is `'error'`, show `online.error` cut short so it fits above the board, `('' + online.error).slice(0, 80)`, at size 12. Then host in one tab, join from a second tab (or a classmate's computer), and race.
hints: You must be signed in and in a class to play online.
The room closes when the host runs the sketch again or leaves the page.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Lab: Trail online". The task: make the race playable across two computers: set up online.onMove once to call takeTurn with the roll in every move, ignoring a move from a seat whose turn it is not or a roll that is not a whole number from 1 to 6; host on a key with a fresh game, or join from a JOIN code; send the roll with online.send instead of applying it when online; let only the player whose seat equals turn roll; and keep offline play working when online.status is off. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.
